newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf says has 66 percent of Leuna.
newsitem.headline: Elf says has 66 percent of Leuna.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine Chairman Philippe Jaffre told a news conference that the French oil group now held 66 percent of the giant Leuna refinery complex, in construction in eastern Germany, after Russian partners did not pay up.
Elf previously had a 43 percent stake.

"We have assumed the 24 percent stake owned by a Russian consortium because the Russians could not pay up their investment in time," Jaffre told a news conference on the 1996 results. He added it remained the aim to find partners for the complex but company officials said this was likely to happen after the refinery was completed.
Leuna is expected to be operational in September/October 1997, the official added.
The other 33 percent of Leuna is still owned by the BvS, the successor of the Truehand privatisation body of former East German assets.
Russia's Rosneft was Elf's main Leuna partner. In November, Russia allowed Rosneft and Megionneftegaz to supply Leuna with 10 million tonnes of crude oil a year to 2010.
BvS is scheduled to buy back a 33 percent stake in a holding company through which Elf owns its stake in Leuna. Last year there was a dispute over the costs of construction.

Elf officials said this dispute had no longer major proportions and was now down to technical differences. Thy said that the construction costs were bigger than forecasts due to the strict environmental rules applied in Germany.
Leuna's original investment called for 5.2 billion marks, with further investments by other companies and the BvS in related chemical plants.
